ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a five-membered ring structure, and has several curved arrows; ignore these arrows according to the problem statement. The left ring atom is a carbon, connected to R1, and forms a double bond with the upper N and a single bond with the lower O. N is further connected to the upper carbon, which is labeled with H and R2. This upper carbon is connected to the right carbon; the right carbon is connected to R3 and OH, and connected to the O in the ring, thereby closing the five-membered ring. Reasoning: Convert R1, R2, and R3 all to wildcard *. According to the specified method, start from the left imine/imino ester carbon as ring atom C1: R1 as * is connected to this carbon, obtaining *C1; this carbon and N are a double bond, written as *C1=N; continue via N to the carbon bearing R2, written as NC(*); then to the right carbon bearing R3 and OH, written as C(*)(O); finally close back to C1 via the ring oxygen atom, written as O1. Combining gives SMILES: *C1=NC(*)C(*)(O)O1.

method.method_draft: First describe the image connectivity, ignoring all curved arrows. Convert R1, R2, and R3 to wildcard substituents '*'. Choose the left imidate carbon as SMILES ring atom C1: attach wildcard R1 to it, write its double bond to N as '*C1=N', continue around the ring through N to the upper carbon bearing R2 as 'NC(*)', then to the right carbon bearing R3 and OH as 'C(*)(O)', then to the ring oxygen closing back to atom 1 as 'O1'. Combine these pieces to obtain '*C1=NC(*)C(*)(O)O1'.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中是一个五元环状结构，并带有若干弯曲箭头；按题意忽略这些箭头。左侧环原子是一个碳，连有 R1，并与上方 N 形成双键、与下方 O 成单键。N 再连到上方的碳，该碳标有 H 和 R2。这个上方碳连到右侧碳；右侧碳连有 R3 和 OH，并连到环中的 O，从而闭合五元环。
推理：把 R1、R2、R3 都转换为通配符 *。按指定方法从左侧亚胺/亚胺酸酯碳作为环原子 C1 开始：R1 作为 * 连在该碳上，得到 *C1；该碳与 N 是双键，写作 *C1=N；继续经 N 到带 R2 的碳，写作 NC(*)；再到带 R3 和 OH 的右侧碳，写作 C(*)(O)；最后经环氧原子闭合回 C1，写作 O1。合并得到 SMILES：*C1=NC(*)C(*)(O)O1。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: Direct graph-to-SMILES route: extract the molecular connectivity from the drawing, ignore the curved arrows, replace each R group with a wildcard atom, then encode the resulting ring in SMILES. This is the natural single robust method for this structure-recognition task.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the image as a five-membered heterocycle: a left ring carbon bearing R1 is double-bonded to N and single-bonded to ring O; N is bonded to the upper carbon bearing H and R2; that carbon is bonded to the right carbon bearing R3 and OH; the right carbon is bonded to the ring O. Curved arrows are present but explicitly ignored.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question instruction to select the SMILES expression for the transition-state structure and to ignore the arrows; no other textual chemical data are needed.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use standard skeletal-structure conventions: unlabeled vertices are carbons, explicit N/O/OH are heteroatoms, R1/R2/R3 substituents can be represented as wildcard atoms '*', hydrogens on carbon need not be written explicitly in SMILES, and ring closure digits encode cyclic bonds. Preserve the C=N double bond shown in the image.
